name: France
headline: A strong state, a single market, and a debt to watch.
summary: France built its power on a centralizing state, a solid civil service, and European integration. Its social model protects and stabilizes, but it is costly: public debt and political fragmentation have become the two variables markets watch most closely.

history.title: French Revolution
history.text: The end of the old monarchical order establishes equality before the law and national sovereignty. The centralized state inherits a strong capacity for mobilization.

history.title: Social reconstruction
history.text: After the war, France creates Social Security and launches indicative planning. The state becomes an investor and coordinates reconstruction.

history.title: The Fifth Republic
history.text: De Gaulle gives the president stable power and an independent diplomacy. The 1958 Constitution remains the current institutional framework.

history.title: Maastricht Treaty
history.text: France commits to the single currency. It loses control of its key rate but gains the credibility of the euro and a market of 450 million consumers.

history.title: Switch to the euro
history.text: The franc disappears. The Eurosystem becomes the real monetary pilot; the Banque de France keeps supervision and financial stability.

history.title: Political fragmentation
history.text: The dissolution of the National Assembly opens a period of government instability. French spreads drift away from Germany's, a sign of a political risk premium.

institutions.executive: President elected for 5 years; Prime Minister accountable to the National Assembly
institutions.central_bank: Banque de France, member of the Eurosystem; ECB for monetary policy
institutions.law: Civil law, Napoleonic Code, strong administrative tradition
institutions.fact: France is the euro area's second-largest economy and one of its leading sovereign-debt issuers.

allies.name: Germany
allies.note: Engine of European integration and industrial partner.

allies.name: European Union
allies.note: Single market, common rules, and recovery funds.

rivals.name: United Kingdom
rivals.note: Post-Brexit financial competition and fishing disputes.

rivals.name: China
rivals.note: Industrial and commercial rival, notably in electric vehicles.

dependencies.name: Germany
dependencies.note: Industrial value chains and the German trade surplus.

dependencies.name: China
dependencies.note: Components, rare earths, and demand for luxury goods.

dependencies.name: Energy imports
dependencies.note: Oil, gas, and uranium must be secured.

gdp_growth.note: Growth is sluggish: investment and exports lack momentum, while consumption holds up thanks to disinflation.

inflation.note: Inflation is back near the ECB target. Falling energy prices did most of the work.

debt_gdp.note: Debt is well above the euro-area average. The high deficit and rising interest costs reduce the room for maneuver.

policy_rate.note: The ECB eases after the 2023 peak. France is subject to monetary policy calibrated for the whole euro area.

unemployment.note: Unemployment remains higher than Germany's, with a core of long-term joblessness and wide regional gaps.

reserves.note: Reserves support euro stability and the Eurosystem's safety net. France does not rely on them to fund itself.

rating.note: The rating remains solid, but the fiscal path is the agencies' main point of concern.

cds.note: Perceived risk stays low. The gap with Germany, however, widened with the political uncertainty of 2024.

equity_index.note: The index suffers from exposure to Chinese luxury demand and political uncertainty, despite banks and energy.

currency.name: Euro
currency.note: The euro is a solid reserve currency, but its rate against the dollar remains sensitive to US rates.

strengths: Productivity, demographics, and a high level of education.
A central position in the single market and appeal to foreign investment.
risks: Public debt and budget deficit with no clear political majority.
Loss of industrial competitiveness against China and the United States.
opportunities: Decarbonized energy and the appeal of data centers.
The Paris financial center strengthened by Brexit.

quiz.question: Which treaty committed France to the European single currency?
quiz.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty (1992) creates the European Union and organizes convergence toward the euro. The single currency starts circulating in 2002.
